t.E500.agn: In 1965, JECFA set the ADI for sodium carbonate and sodium hydrogen carbonate (bicarbonate) as 'not limited'. In the EU, as a Group I additive, it may be used at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E500.body: Its sodium, like sodium from food, is almost completely absorbed in the gut (about 98%); the amount in the body is regulated mainly by the kidneys, which excrete the excess in the urine.
t.E500.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E500.prod: It may be obtained from natural mineral deposits or by chemical production.
t.E500.pw.0: It is a source of sodium. Sodium from additives is usually less than sodium from salt.
t.E500.regx.0: ADI 'not limited' for sodium carbonate and sodium hydrogen carbonate.
t.E500.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E500.summary: Sodium carbonate and sodium bicarbonate (carbonate). It is the main component of baking powder; it raises dough and regulates acidity.
t.E500.what: Sodium carbonate and sodium bicarbonate (baking soda); used as a raising agent, acidity regulator and buffer.
